entities.name: Marcus Peducaeus Priscinus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcus Peducaeus Priscinus was a Roman senator of the second century, known for his role as ordinary consul in 110 CE alongside Servius Cornelius Scipio Salvidienus Orfitus.

 Born into a prominent equestrian family, Priscinus rose through the ranks of the Roman Senate, becoming a key figure in the imperial administration of the Roman Empire.

 His significance lies in his contribution to the Roman Senate, where he played a part in shaping imperial policy and securing the continued expansion of the Roman state.
